found_without_a_rule: Metropolis warrant 2024-09-30 published 6,314 units for a printed and tagged 4 (fixed above). Cause is shared: the unit-scale normaliser in pipeline/unified_holdings.py compares price per unit across all rows of one issuer (cik + issuer_name), so a warrant beside a preferred of the same issuer is read as a scale outlier and given the neighbour's count. Not changed (shared code); other funds not measured.

Protective Industrial Products Series A Preferred, 2023-12-31: the page prints 31,597 and the share-count fact is 31597; published shares_held is 31 (same normaliser, labelled derived_proxy). The filer prints the figure in two scales (30, 31, 31, then 31,597, then 33 to 38), so neither value is clearly right; left as is.

The 'Par Amount / Shares' figure on the PIK preferred rows is an amount in thousands of dollars, not a count: Metropolis Class B 6,314 / 6,950 / 7,535 / 8,162 and Class A 18,041 / 19,184 / 20,166 grow at the PIK rate, and Protective 30 to 38 is in millions. Where the filer tagged it with the share-count concept (2024-09-30, 2024-12-31, Protective to 2024-12-31) it is published as shares_held: as filed, but a reader will take 18,041 for a number of shares.

The earlier reading (docs/investigations/v05_readings/0001849894.md, C04 row) says the printed units are tagged as a principal amount; for the preferred rows that is a par amount correctly tagged as principal, and only the warrant (4) and Class D (24) look like counts.
The two declared pars carry principal_amount_source 'xbrl_field' although the value comes from the page, not from a fact of that context (label written by the shared declared-value path).
